# k0rdent_vpc_peering (Resource)

One side of a peering between two VPCs in the same region.

**Creating this does not connect anything on its own.** The project that owns `remote_vpc` has to declare its own mirrored peering pointing back, and until it does the peering is half-open. That is a normal state, not an error, and this side's `state` can't show it. The mirror is listed under `remote_vpc`, so after a create the provider lists that VPC's peerings: when it finds an `active` one pointing back it says nothing, and otherwise it warns, saying what it found. It reads only a `remote_vpc` in this peering's own region and project. For one anywhere else, or one whose read is refused, the warning says so and the far side has to be confirmed out of band.

**A peering outlives the VPC it points at.** If the remote VPC's owning cluster is deleted, this object survives, still `active`, naming a VPC that is gone, carrying no traffic. The platform will not remove it on the strength of another project's delete. Destroying it, or destroying the owner of the local VPC, is what clears it.

Requires `region` and `project` on the provider.

**What replaces it.** Changing `description`, `display_name`, `id`, `project`, `region`, `remote_vpc`, `tags` or `vpc` cannot be done in place and replaces the peering. Everything else changes in place.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Take the VPC from the cluster that made it, not from a data source. A data
# source can become unknown when the cluster changes, which would replace
# this peering.
locals {
  training_vpc = k0rdent_kubernetes_cluster.training.vpc
}

# A VPC in this project goes in remote_vpc by id, such as
# k0rdent_instance_group.hosts.vpc. One in another project needs its
# `self_link`. Read it here if you can read that project, or have its own
# configuration output it.
data "k0rdent_vpc" "inference" {
  project = "inference"
  id      = "vpc-inference"
}

# This is one side. Traffic flows only once the other project adds a peering
# back. Until then this one still shows `active`, with no error.
resource "k0rdent_vpc_peering" "to_inference" {
  id  = "to-inference"
  vpc = local.training_vpc

  remote_vpc = data.k0rdent_vpc.inference.self_link

  display_name = "Training to inference"

  # Set only at creation, like the provider's `default_tags` here. Later
  # changes are ignored, with a warning in the plan.
  tags = {
    team = "ml-platform"
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `remote_vpc` (String) The counterpart VPC: its id, for one in this peering's own region and project, or its `self_link`, for one anywhere else.

Name a VPC in the same project by id, through the `vpc` attribute of the cluster or instance group that brought it. That stays known while the owner changes, so renaming it replaces no peering. A `self_link` read from the `k0rdent_vpc` data source does not: Terraform reads the data source during the apply when the owner has a change pending, and a value it doesn't know at plan replaces the peering. The provider sends an id as the URI the API takes, built from the contract's path for a VPC. Moving between an id and the `self_link` of the same VPC replaces nothing.

It must be an `active` VPC in the same region, and not the local one. It may be in a project you have no permission on, because declaring this side is not by itself enough to establish the peering. **Can force replacement**: replaces the peering unless the new value names the same VPC. **Constraints:** An id must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen. A self_link is sent as written.
- `vpc` (String) Id of the local VPC this peering is declared under. Find it with the `k0rdent_vpcs` data source: a VPC is materialized by a cluster or instance group, never created directly. **Forces replacement**. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free-form text describing it, for people to read. **Forces replacement**.
- `display_name` (String) Human-friendly name. The API has no update for a peering, so even this can't change in place. **Forces replacement**.
- `id` (String) Peering name, unique within the project. Omit it and the provider generates one, `tf-` and 16 hex digits, so that a create whose answer is lost can be read back rather than sent twice. **Forces replacement**. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL. String length must be at most 63.
- `project` (String) Project this resource belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project`. It's part of the resource's API path, so a resource can't move between projects. **Forces replacement**. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `region` (String) Region this resource lives in. Defaults to the provider's `region`. It's part of the resource's API path, so a resource can't move between regions. **Forces replacement**. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `tags` (Map of String) User-defined labels, settable only at creation. **Can force replacement**: replaces the resource when the tags the platform would hold change, and not when it writes out a tag the provider's `default_tags` already supplies with the same value, or leaves one there. **Constraints:** The key `terraform-provider-k0rdent/create-token` is the provider's own.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) How long each operation may take before it fails. Each operation left out defaults to the provider's `operation_timeout`, which is `2h` unless the provider block or `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` sets it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `local_vpc` (String) URI of the local VPC, as the platform resolved it from `vpc`. Always in this resource's own project.
- `self_link` (String) Platform-defined reference to this peering.
- `state` (String) Lifecycle state **of this side only**. `active` means this declaration is applied on the fabric. It says nothing about whether the counterpart has been declared or whether traffic flows.
- `tags_all` (Map of String) Every tag the platform holds for this resource: the provider's `default_tags` with this resource's own `tags` on top, a resource tag winning over a default with the same key. Known at plan whenever both are, so the plan shows the result. The provider's create token never appears here. The API sets a peering's tags only at creation, so a change to the provider's `default_tags` reaches a new peering and leaves one that exists as it is, with a warning in the plan.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) Bounds the whole create, including the wait until the platform reports it ready. Left out, it defaults to the provider's `operation_timeout`, which is `2h` unless the provider block or `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` sets it. **Constraints:** Must be a positive duration of hours, minutes or seconds, such as `45m`, `2h` or `1h30m`.
- `delete` (String) Bounds the whole destroy, including the wait until the platform reports it gone. Left out, it defaults to the provider's `operation_timeout`, which is `2h` unless the provider block or `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` sets it. **Constraints:** Must be a positive duration of hours, minutes or seconds, such as `45m`, `2h` or `1h30m`.

## Timeouts

The `timeouts` block sets how long each operation may take before it fails:

- `create` (default `2h`). Bounds the whole create, including the wait until the platform reports it ready.
- `delete` (default `2h`). Bounds the whole destroy, including the wait until the platform reports it gone.

Each default is the provider's `operation_timeout`, which is `2h` unless the provider block or `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` sets it. An operation the block leaves out takes that value, so raising `operation_timeout` raises all of them at once. A value of zero or less is refused at plan time rather than read as no limit.

A wait that runs out, or a run that is interrupted, stops nothing on the platform. A create that stops waiting fails, and Terraform taints the object: run `terraform untaint` on it and then `terraform apply`, which waits for the same object. A delete that stops waiting fails and stays in state, and the next `terraform destroy` waits for the same delete without sending another.

```terraform
resource "k0rdent_vpc_peering" "example" {
  # ...

  timeouts {
    create = "45m"
    delete = "45m"
  }
}
```

## Related

- [`k0rdent_vpc_peering`](../data-sources/vpc_peering.md) data source: reads one this configuration doesn't manage.
- [`k0rdent_vpc_peering`](../list-resources/vpc_peering.md) list resource: finds every one, for `terraform query` to adopt.
- [`k0rdent_vpc`](../data-sources/vpc.md) data source: reads a VPC's `self_link`, which `remote_vpc` takes for one in another project.
- [`k0rdent_vpcs`](../data-sources/vpcs.md) data source: lists the VPCs `vpc` and `remote_vpc` name.
- [`k0rdent_kubernetes_cluster`](../resources/kubernetes_cluster.md) resource: materializes the VPC a peering is declared under.
- [`k0rdent_instance_group`](../resources/instance_group.md) resource: materializes a VPC too, whose `vpc` a peering in this project takes as `remote_vpc`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# The same address with each part named. Leave out region and project to
# use the provider's.
import {
  to = k0rdent_vpc_peering.example
  identity = {
    region  = "us-texas-1"
    project = "cp-production"
    vpc     = "vpc-training"
    id      = "to-inference"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) The resource's id.
- `vpc` (String) Id of the VPC this resource lives under.

#### Optional

- `project` (String) Project the resource lives in. Defaults to the provider's `project` on import.
- `region` (String) Region the resource lives in. Defaults to the provider's `region` on import.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# Takes every id form `terraform import` does. A peering is addressed under
# its local VPC. The first command below names that VPC, the second names the
# scope too.
import {
  to = k0rdent_vpc_peering.example
  id = "us-texas-1/cp-production/vpc-training/to-inference"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import k0rdent_vpc_peering.example vpc-training/to-inference

terraform import k0rdent_vpc_peering.example us-texas-1/cp-production/vpc-training/to-inference
```
